_note: Single source of truth for Line of Command V1 balance numbers. spec.md quotes these values; if they disagree, this file wins and spec.md is the bug.
status: DECIDED 2026-11-22 (captain): Hold the Fort in V1 at a 47% target (band 44-50%); the Systems Designer added Last Stand at 35% (band 32-38%) as a harder step.

rules.daily: v1.1: a scenario is played as a ranked battle only by taking a scenario assignment from the daily board (campaign.json). That uses 1 of the 3 daily ranked battles and gives normal progress (Wisdom x wisdom_win_mult on a win, skills, attribute roll, rank counts, reveals, breeding-eligibility count). Every other scenario play is a replay: free, unlimited, no progress, no battle used.

hold_the_fort.name: Hold the Fort
hold_the_fort.blurb: A young officer and a small garrison hold a stone fort against the vanguard of a much larger column. Real forts were stormed at three to six attackers per defender; you face the leading brigade, and the rest of the column is still on the road.

objective.defender_wins_if: not routed and (tick >= hold_ticks or attacker strength < (1 - attacker_loss_fraction) x attacker S)
objective.attacker_wins_if: defender routs or is eliminated first
objective.check: after the rout check (tick step 5); a defender rout is checked first

hold_the_fort.historical_odds_note: text only (v1.3): real assaults came at about 3-6 attackers per defender (Yorktown Redoubt 10, 1781, about 6:1 and taken; Fort Wagner, 1863, about 2.8:1 and repulsed). The battle itself stays 14 vs 10 points; the briefing and narration tell the larger odds as story. Literal 3:1 would need walls x0.23 and a 30-point attacker (historian-assessment.md).

rewards.formula: min(2, 0.5 / target_defender_win_rate), applied to Wisdom gain on a win only; a loss uses the normal x1.25

last_stand.name: Last Stand
last_stand.blurb: The same garrison behind a broken earthwork, with the column's vanguard already at the ditch. Fort Wagner (1863) held at nearly three to one. Hold out for twelve turns.
